topic: Why every Indian party has a picture symbol (30-second sample)
method: Reference and press summaries via web search, cross-checked; the 1952 photograph and the EVM photograph are primary records; Election Commission figures for 2024.

claims.claim: India's first general election, held in 1951-52, had about 173 million registered voters.

sources.title: Business Standard: Remembering India's first general election (19 April 2024)
sources.quote: 173.2 million voters, excluding Jammu and Kashmir, were registered

contradictions: Some sources give about 176 million (different scope).

claims.claim: About 18 per cent of Indians could read at the 1951 census.

sources.title: Drishti IAS: First General Election 1951-52 (13 April 2024)
Census of India 1951 literacy (Wikipedia: Literacy in India)

claims.claim: In 1951-52 each candidate had a separate ballot box at the polling station, marked with the candidate's election symbol; voters dropped their ballot paper into the box of their choice.

sources.title: 1951–52 Indian general election (Wikipedia)
sources.quote: separate ballot boxes for each candidate with the candidate's symbol

sources.title: Drishti IAS: First General Election 1951-52 (13 April 2024)
sources.quote: separate ballot boxes for each candidate at all booths, with the candidate's election symbol on it

sources.title: Wikimedia Commons: Indian election 1952 ballot boxes (photograph)
sources.quote: [the photograph] a row of ballot boxes, each with a picture symbol

claims.claim: Indian voters today vote on electronic voting machines, whose ballot unit shows each candidate's name and party symbol beside a button.

sources.title: Election Commission of India: EVM (FAQ)
sources.quote: ballot unit ... name and symbol of candidates

sources.title: Electronic voting in India (Wikipedia)
sources.quote: the ballot unit lists candidates' names and symbols

claims.claim: The 2024 Lok Sabha election had about 980 million (97.98 crore) registered electors, according to Election Commission data.

sources.title: Drishti IAS: Data of Lok Sabha Elections 2024
